info.name: PayWay API — Complete Collection
info.description:
# 🚀 PayWay API — Get Started

**Welcome!** This collection is a complete playground for the [PayWay merchant APIs](https://developer.payway.com.kh/). It ships **pre-configured with this project's sandbox merchant credentials** (merchant `ec476910`), so your first request works immediately — no extra setup.

> **While testing:** open the Postman **Console** (bottom-left). Every request logs its `b4hash:` signing string there so you can verify it against the docs. 
  

---

## 1 · Your first transaction (60 seconds, zero setup)

1. Open **03 - Ecommerce Checkout → 1. Purchase (Hosted Checkout)** → hit **Send**.
    
2. Open the **Visualize** tab of the response → click **Open payment page →**.  
    The button form-POSTs your signed fields and the checkout page is served by PayWay itself — no CORS problems.
    
3. Pay with the sandbox test card:
    
    | Card | Number | Expiry | CVV | 3-D Secure |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | ✅ Success | `4286 0900 0000 0206` | 04/30 | 777 | Yes (any code) |
    | ✅ Success (no 3DS) | `5156 8399 3770 6777` | 01/30 | 993 | No |
    | ❌ Declined | `5156 8302 7256 1029` | 04/30 | 777 | Yes |
    
4. Back in Postman, send **3\. Check Transaction** → `payment_status_code: 0 (APPROVED)` 🎉
    

That is the whole merchant lifecycle you are learning: **create → host the page → verify**.

> 💡 **Helper text everywhere:** every request's description starts with a **⚡ Quick test** block — what to set (usually nothing), what you'll see, and what to send next. After key responses the **Console** also prints a `NEXT:` hint. 
  

## 2 · What happens automatically

- **Chaining** — every response saves what the next request needs: `{{last_tran_id}}`, `{{pwt}}`, `{{ctid}}`, `{{request_id}}`, `{{payment_link_id}}`. Just send requests in the documented order.
    
- **Signing** — every pre-request builds `hash = base64(HMAC-SHA512(field values in documented order, secret_key))` and logs the exact input as `b4hash:`. Amounts are formatted per `{{currency}}`: USD 2 decimals, KHR integer.
    
- **Polling** — **11 - Polling & Lifecycle Flows → Flow A** loops on `data.payment_status_code` while it is `2 (PENDING)`, budgeted by `{{max_polls}}`. Run the folder in the **Collection Runner** (delay ≥ 1000 ms).
    
- **Callbacks** — folder **10** documents payment/token payloads + `X-PayWay-Hmac-Sha512` verification, can replay samples to `{{callback_listener}}`, and can **pull** callbacks back from webhook.site into your variables.
    
- **RSA endpoints** (Refund, Payment Link, Pre-auth, Payout, Whitelist) encrypt `merchant_auth`/`beneficiaries` with the self-contained PKCS#1 v1.5 helper and Postman's secure random source. No library installation or package download is needed.
    
- **Prerequisite guards** — requests that need earlier state (`{{pwt}}`, `{{request_id}}`, `{{last_tran_id}}`) stop with a clear message telling you exactly which request to run first.
    

## 3 · Pick your journey

| You want to… | Go to |
| --- | --- |
| Take a card / ABA Pay / wallet payment | **03 - Ecommerce Checkout** |
| Show a QR to scan (ABA app) | **04 - ABA QR API**, then poll with **Flow A** in **11** |
| Link a card/account, charge later | **08 - Credentials on File (CoF)** |
| Sell via a shareable link | **05 - Payment Link** |
| Hold funds, capture or release later | **06 - Pre-auth** |
| Split payments to beneficiaries | **07 - Payout** |
| Look up KHQR payments by merchant ref | **09 - KHQR Guideline** |
| Test your webhook handling | **10 - Callbacks & Webhooks** |

## 4 · Switching to your own merchant (before real integration)

| Variable | Replace with | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{merchant_id}}` | Your sandbox merchant ID | From PayWay onboarding |
| `{{secret_key}}` | Your sandbox secret | Stored as a **Postman secret** type — masked in UI/exports |
| `{{rsa_public_key}}` | Your RSA public key (PEM) | Needed by the RSA endpoints above |
| `{{ctid}}` | Your consumer ID | CoF folders |
| `{{baseUrl}}` | `https://checkout.payway.com.kh` | Production only |

> ⚠️ The pre-filled demo credentials are **public** — use them only to explore. Replace them before touching anything real, and never commit your secret into source control. 
  

## 5 · Transaction statuses

`data.payment_status_code`: **0** APPROVED / PRE-AUTH · **2** PENDING · **3** DECLINED · **4** REFUNDED · **7** CANCELLED

Gateway `status.code` is `"00"`/`0` on success and otherwise an error code (string _or_ number) — test scripts normalize both. Most common errors:

| Code | Meaning |  | Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Wrong hash |  | 5 | Transaction not found |
| 4 | Given data was invalid |  | 6 | Domain not whitelisted |
| 2 | Invalid transaction ID |  | 12 | Currency not allowed |
| 4 | Duplicated transaction ID |  | 47 | KHR must be ≥ 100 |
| 23 | Payment option not enabled |  | 429 | Rate limit exceeded |
| PTL02 | Wrong hash (portal APIs) |  | 503 | Under maintenance |

Full table: [developer.payway.com.kh](https://developer.payway.com.kh/) · `b4hash:` in the Console is your first stop for any `Wrong hash`.

## 6 · 60-second fixes

The five snags that cost developers the most time, with the one-line fix:

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Wrong hash` (code 1) | Open the **Console** → compare the `b4hash:` line with the docs' field order (each request's description lists it too). USD amounts need 2 decimals, KHR none — the scripts handle this via `fmtAmt`. |
| RSA endpoints answer `SKIPPED` | Ensure the Postman runtime supports `crypto.getRandomValues`; or paste a fresh pre-encrypted value into the fallback variable named in the request. |
| Code 5 / transaction not found | `check-transaction-2` only sees the **last 7 days** and **no KHQR** transactions — use **2\. Get Transaction Details** instead. |
| Code 49 Invalid Start Date | Transaction List dates must be `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss` (auto-filled for you — don't shorten them). |
| Code 23 payment option not enabled | The demo profile doesn't allow that wallet — switch `{{payment_option}}` (try `cards` or `abapay_khqr`). |

## 7 · Environments

- **Sandbox (default):** `https://checkout-sandbox.payway.com.kh`
    
- **Production:** `https://checkout.payway.com.kh` — only after replacing the demo credentials
    
- **Docs:** [developer.payway.com.kh](https://developer.payway.com.kh/)

item.name: 03 - Ecommerce Checkout
item.description:
## Ecommerce Checkout
REST endpoints for the standard hosted-checkout flow (cards, ABA KHQR, wallets).

**Suggested order:**
1. **Purchase** - creates a transaction and returns a hosted page; save the `tran_id` (auto-stored in `{{last_tran_id}}`).
2. **Check Transaction** - fast status check while a customer pays (great for polling).
3. **Get Transaction Details** - full record.
4. **Close Transaction** / **Refund** - close or money-back (Refund needs RSA).
5. **Transaction List** / **Exchange Rate** - admin views.

All hashes follow `req_time + merchant_id + tran_id + ...` per endpoint (see each description).

item.name: 04 - ABA QR API
item.description:
## ABA QR API

`POST /generate-qr` creates an ABA KHQR for static/dynamic payment. Render `qr_data` as a QR image, or show `qr_image`. The payer scans with the ABA app.

After payment, verify via **Check Transaction** or the callback. The purchase_type/payment_option both default to `{{payment_option}}`.

request.description:
## ⚡ Quick test
1. Just hit **Send** → the **Visualize** tab renders the scannable KHQR + raw `qrString`.
2. Scan with the ABA Mobile app, then poll **Flow A (folder 11)** or use **2. Get Transaction Details** — *Check Transaction cannot see QR transactions*.

## Generate QR
Hash order: `req_time, merchant_id, tran_id, amount, items, first_name, last_name, email, phone, purchase_type, payment_option, callback_url, return_deeplink, currency, custom_fields, return_params, payout, lifetime, qr_image_template`.

- `purchase_type` allows only `purchase` or `pre-auth` (sandbox-verified 2026-09). The wallet selector is `payment_option`: `abapay_khqr` (QR static), `abapay_khqr_deeplink`, `abapay`, `abapay_deeplink`, `cards`, `alipay`, `wechat`.
- `callback_url` is base64-encoded (auto).
- Field `account_information` may be passed to override the default QR account.
- Response (sandbox-verified): `qrString` = KHQR string to render as a QR image; `qrImage` = base64 PNG data-URL of the templated QR.

item.name: 05 - Payment Link

## Payment Link

Create a shareable payment link (sent via WhatsApp/email/SMS), query its stats, and void (permanently cancel) an unpaid link - void is IRREVERSIBLE and kills the hosted page for customers (code 07 shell).

> These are **portal APIs**: instead of a plain hash they require `merchant_auth` = base64 of the RSA-encrypted payload. The collection's versioned portable helper handles encryption; if secure randomness is unavailable, paste a pre-encrypted value into `{{pl_merchant_auth}}`.

request.description:
## Create Payment Link
RSA payload: `{ "mc_id": "...", "title": "...", "amount": "...", "currency": "...", "description": "...", "payment_limit": "...", "expired_date": 1234567890, "return_url": "base64...", "merchant_ref_no": "...", "payout": Array|null }`
Hash: `request_time + merchant_id + merchant_auth`.

- `expired_date` is a future Unix timestamp in seconds (this request defaults to seven days from now).
- `return_url` inside the RSA payload must be **base64-encoded exactly once**. `{{return_url}}` accepts a plain HTTPS URL or its base64 form.
- RSA encryption runs inside this collection with no package download. If secure randomness is unavailable, set `{{pl_merchant_auth}}` with the pre-encrypted payload.
- On success, open the **Visualization** tab to copy or open the hosted payment link. The response also saves `data.id` as `{{payment_link_id}}` for Detail and Void.

```php
$data = json_encode($payload);
openssl_public_encrypt($data, $enc, $key, OPENSSL_PKCS1_PADDING);
$merchant_auth = base64_encode($enc);
```

item.name: 07 - Payout
item.description:
## Payout
Mass payouts (up to 250 beneficiaries) plus the whitelist that authorities them.

**Sequence:** whitelist the payee account first, then send a payout. Both need RSA (folder 06 variables). Payout hashes use the **body beneficiaries ciphertext** as a hash input, so the hash must be computed AFTER encryption.

2. RSA encryption runs inside this collection with no package download; `{{payout_beneficiaries}}` is the manual fallback. Per-beneficiary minimum: USD 0.01 / KHR 100.

`beneficiaries` is the **base64 of the RSA-encrypted** array `[{"account":"...","amount":"..."}, ...]` (max 250).
Hash order: `merchant_id, tran_id, beneficiaries, amount, custom_fields, currency`.

- `amount` here is the merchant's payout total string.
- Every account must already be whitelisted (folder 07 requests 2/3).
- Min per beneficiary: USD 0.01 / KHR 100.
If secure randomness is unavailable, set `{{payout_beneficiaries}}` (paste base64).

```php
$data = json_encode([['account'=>'...','amount'=>'...'],['account'=>'...','amount'=>'...']]);
openssl_public_encrypt($data, $enc, $key, OPENSSL_PKCS1_PADDING);
$beneficiaries = base64_encode($enc);
```

item.description:
## Credentials on File (CoF) / Subscriptions
Tokenize a card or ABA account, then charge it later without re-entering credentials.

**Typical flow:** `1. Link Account` (or `2. Link Card`) -> wait for callback -> `3. Get Token Details` (auto-saves `{{pwt}}`/`{{ctid}}`) -> `4. Payment` -> `6. Remove` at the end.

`callback_url` must be base64-encoded in the hash/body - the scripts do that automatically for https URLs. Run `7. Subscription` to test recurring CITR_FIX payments.

item.description:
## KHQR Guideline - offline KHQR generation (local build -> scan -> webhook -> inquiry)
Build the KHQR payload **entirely in Postman scripts** per the PayWay KHQR guideline (EMVCo TLV + CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE) - no generate-qr call, no per-QR API dependency. Full flow:

1. **Create webhook.site Receiver** - fresh pushback catcher (or paste your own bin into `{{callback_listener}}`).
2. **Build Offline KHQR (TLV + CRC + QR)** - unique merchant reference per send, payload self-tested against the guideline's official sample, QR rendered on the **Visualize** tab. Pay with any KHQR app.
3. **Pull webhook.site Callbacks (KHQR)** - import the pushback (transaction id + payment status).
4. **Get Transactions by Merchant Ref** - inquiry/recovery path by the same reference (works even when the callback is missed).

> **Caveats:** offline KHQR has **no per-QR callback** - the pushback goes to the webhook URL provisioned on your merchant account (point it at webhook.site); KHQR lookups by reference need KHQR retrieval provisioned on the profile (demo profiles observe 404 - the request itself is docs-verified); a KHQR **can be paid multiple times** - deduplicate by `transaction_id`, reconcile by `merchant_ref`.

item.name: 10 - Callbacks & Webhooks
item.description:
## Callbacks & Webhooks
Everything PayWay POSTs back to **your** server, plus how to verify it.

- Set `{{callback_listener}}` (e.g. webhook.site) and these sample senders will POST real-looking payloads to it.
- The `X-PayWay-Hmac-Sha512` header is computed with the same ksort+concat rule PayWay uses, so you can test your verifier end-to-end.
- 'Webhook Design Notes' summarises idempotency / retry / response guidance.

## How to get a callback URL
Postman has no built-in inbound URL; you provide one.

1. **Free webhook catcher (easiest)** - open **webhook.site** (or webhookbin.com), copy its `https://webhook.site/<uuid>` URL, and paste it into `{{callback_url}}`, `{{cof_callback_url}}` and `{{callback_listener}}`. PayWay/sample senders will POST results there and you watch payloads arrive in the browser.
   - While PayWay does not push straight into Postman, you **can sync webhook.site -> Postman**: webhook.site exposes a REST API. `GET https://api.webhook.site/token/<uuid>/requests` returns every received payload as JSON. A dedicated Postman request can call that endpoint and, in its test script, save `pwt`/`ctid`/`tran_id` from the latest callback into collection variables - effectively importing the callback. (webhookbin has no such API; use webhook.site for the sync trick.)
2. **Postman Mock Server (closest Postman-native)** - create a mock server for this collection in the Postman web UI; it issues a public `https://<mock-id>.mock.pstmn.io` URL that accepts any POST and returns your mock response. The **Call Logs** tab shows every received callback (headers + body) so you can read `pwt`/`tran_id` there.
3. **ngrok + local listener** - `ngrok http 8080` pointed at a local web server; set `{{callback_url}}` to the ngrok URL. Best when you want to script saving variables or run a verifier locally.

> Tip: for the CoF workflows (folders 08 / 11) the callback is optional - request `3. Get Token Details` already fetches and saves `pwt`/`ctid` from the API using `{{request_id}}`.

request.description:
## Payment callback
PayWay POSTs this JSON to your `callback_url` (or profile pushback URL) and signs it:
```
X-PayWay-Hmac-Sha512: base64(HMAC-SHA512(<concat>, {{secret_key}}))
```
- Sort the payload keys ascending (`apv, return_params, status, tran_id`) as they arrived, **concat values** (arrays/objects are json_encoded), HMAC-SHA512, Base64, then compare with `hash_equals` against the header.
- `apv` auto-generated approval code; `status` 0/2/3/4/7; `return_params` echoes what you sent.

This request posts a **sample** to `{{callback_listener}}` (set it to webhook.site) so you can inspect the raw wire format.

// Compute X-PayWay-Hmac-Sha512 exactly as PayWay does: sorted keys, concat values, HMAC-SHA512, base64.
if (typeof v === 'string' || typeof v === 'number') return String(v);

request.description:
## Webhook checklist
1. **Verify every callback** with `X-PayWay-Hmac-Sha512` (see folder 09 for the exact algorithm).
2. **Idempotency**: use `tran_id` / `request_id` as the unique key in your database; you may receive a callback more than once.
3. **Fast 200**: respond 200 immediately; do heavy processing asynchronously.
4. Return 200 with empty body so PayWay does not retry.
5. PayWay retries failed deliveries (see your profile/incident settings).

item.name: 11 - Polling & Lifecycle Flows (Runner)
item.description:
## Polling & Lifecycle Flows (Collection Runner)
Composable flows via `postman.setNextRequest` - run these from the **Collection Runner** (set delay 1000 ms).

- **Flow A:** Generate QR -> poll until settled -> get details -> refund.
- **Flow B:** Link account -> get token -> charge -> renew -> remove.

Fallback: when run as single requests, each step still saves the variables the next step needs (`{{last_tran_id}}`, `{{pwt}}`, `{{request_id}}`).
